PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 27 years
Gestational Age at Sampling: 17 weeks
Indication for Testing: Prenatal screening for common aneuploidies
Clinical Details: Routine prenatal testing via amniocentesis

TEST PERFORMED
Rapid Aneuploidy Detection by Quantitative Fluorescence PCR (QF-PCR)

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured amniocytes obtained by amniocentesis. Quantitative Fluorescence PCR (QF-PCR) was performed using a panel of polymorphic short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. The following markers were analyzed:

Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1446

PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak area ratios were calculated for each informative marker.

RESULTS

CHROMOSOME 13
Informative markers: 3/4
All markers showed normal biallelic patterns
Peak ratios within normal range (0.8-1.4)
Conclusion: Consistent with two copies of chromosome 13

CHROMOSOME 18
Informative markers: 4/4
All markers showed normal biallelic patterns
Peak ratios within normal range (0.8-1.4)
Conclusion: Consistent with two copies of chromosome 18

CHROMOSOME 21
Informative markers: 3/4
All markers showed normal biallelic patterns
Peak ratios within normal range (0.8-1.4)
Conclusion: Consistent with two copies of chromosome 21

MATERNAL CELL CONTAMINATION
Maternal contamination markers analyzed: Negative
No evidence of significant maternal cell contamination

OVERALL INTERPRETATION
No abnormalities detected. The QF-PCR analysis is consistent with a normal chromosomal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. These results suggest the absence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), and trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in the fetal sample.

LIMITATIONS
This test specifically targets chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only. Other chromosomal abnormalities, including sex chromosome aneuploidies, other autosomal trisomies, structural rearrangements, mosaicism below 20%, and single gene disorders are not detected by this method.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis of cultured amniocytes to follow. This will provide comprehensive cytogenetic evaluation of all chromosomes and can detect structural abnormalities not identified by QF-PCR. Results expected within 10-14 days.

This report has been reviewed and authorized by:

Consultant Clinical Scientist
